children.name: Trithuria brevistyla  de Lange & Mosyakin
children.description: A diminutive, tufted, aquatic herb 10–40 mm tall producing numerous unsheathed, fine hair-like leaves arranged in fans, with inconspicuous inflorescences borne on stalks 1–6 mm long and much-reduced, female-only flowers. Endemic to the South Island of New Zealand, it grows in the shallows of glacial lakes between 35 and 600 m a.s.l., often part of the aquatic-turf community. It differs from T. inconspicua in its shortened stigmatic hairs forming a knobbly capitate head. Classified Threatened – Nationally Vulnerable.
